title: Norm bounds imply low-degree Fourier weight
statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $c\le1$. Suppose $f$ is the threshold sign of a multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$. Suppose also that every coefficient family $p$ of degree at most $k$ satisfies
\[c\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)^2\le\left(\mathbb E_x\left|\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)\chi_S(x)\right|\right)^2,\]
where $x$ is uniform on the Boolean cube and $\chi_S$ is the Walsh character. Then $c\le\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2$, the Fourier weight of $f$ on levels at most $k$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a degree-at-most-$k$ polynomial threshold function
For every coefficient family of degree at most $k$, the stated coefficient-square-sum bound by squared expected absolute polynomial value holds
replaced:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, $c\in\mathbb R$ with $c\le1$, and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ for uniform $x$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
Suppose $f$ is the sign of some real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$, with $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$, and assume that every real polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{|S|\le k}a_S\chi_S(x)$ satisfies
\[
 c\sum_{|S|\le k}a_S^2\le\bigl(\mathbb E_x|p(x)|\bigr)^2.
\]
Then $c\le\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
